bibliographic.title: CodeHelp: Using Large Language Models with Guardrails for Scalable Support in Programming Classes
bibliographic.authors: Mark Liffiton; Brad Sheese; Jaromir Savelka; Paul Denny
bibliographic.citation_apa: Liffiton, M., Sheese, B., Savelka, J., & Denny, P. (2023). CodeHelp: Using large language models with guardrails for scalable support in programming classes. arXiv preprint arXiv:2308.06921.

methodology.sample_description: First-year computer and data science course; student interactions collected over 12 weeks
methodology.technology_context: LLM-powered on-demand programming assistance tool (CodeHelp) with guardrails, prompting pipeline, and instructor-facing observability features

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article clearly addresses an LLM-based interactive support system with explicit guardrails and instructor review/observability in an educational deployment, which is partially aligned with conversational operational governance. However, the provided text emphasizes scalable student support and pedagogical guardrails rather than governance, accountability, audit/compliance, contestation, or regulated high-stakes controls central to the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Borderline fit: strong LLM, conversational assistance, and guardrails signals, but no explicit governance/accountability/compliance framing in the supplied text; full-text sections on instructor oversight, logging, and limitations were not provided.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is based only on front matter and partial excerpts. Deployment parameters (52 students, 12 weeks) are clear, but detailed methods, analysis procedures, ethics approval, and limitations are not visible in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: The study appears internally coherent for evaluating an educational LLM support tool, but supplied evidence is insufficient to judge analysis rigor, ethics, and limitations. Relevance to conversational governance in regulated environments is indirect, mainly via guardrails and instructor oversight.

coding.theme: Guardrailed LLM assistance for programming education
coding.subtheme: Instructor-visible conversational support with solution-avoidance controls

synthesis.main_claim: CodeHelp is an LLM-powered tool with guardrails that provides scalable on-demand programming help without directly revealing solutions, and a 12-week deployment with 52 students suggests positive student reception and instructor usability.
synthesis.contribution: Offers a concrete design for guardrailed LLM educational support, including prompting strategies and instructor-facing features to observe and review student interactions.
synthesis.limitations: Supplied text does not provide full methodological detail, ethics information, or explicit governance/compliance mechanisms; single-course sample limits generalizability.
synthesis.use_in_review: Potentially useful as borderline/supporting evidence on guardrails and instructor oversight in LLM conversational tutoring, but weak direct evidence for governance, accountability, audit, or regulated compliance.
